name: gitflow
description: Gitflow integration and support in Visual Studio Code

gitflow.deleteBranchOnFinish.description: After finishing a branch, delete the branch

gitflow.deleteRemoteBranches.description: If true, and `gitflow.deleteBranchOnFinish` is true, remote branches will be deleted when finishing a branch

gitflow.requireSync.description: 🔒 Synchronization: Require branches to be synchronized with remote before creating features
gitflow.requireSync.markdownDescription:
**🔒 Synchronization Control**

Require branches to be synchronized with remote before creating features. Useful for corporate projects that need strict synchronization.

gitflow.allowOfflineWork.description: 🌐 Offline Work: Allow creating features without checking remote synchronization
gitflow.allowOfflineWork.markdownDescription:
**🌐 Offline Work Support**

Allow creating features without checking remote synchronization. Perfect for working without internet connection or when remotes are temporarily unavailable.

gitflow.default.development.description: 🌿 Branch Names: Default name for the development branch
gitflow.default.development.markdownDescription:
**🌿 Default Branch Names**

Default name for the development branch. Usually 'develop' or 'main' depending on your team's convention.

gitflow.default.production.description: 🌿 Branch Names: Default name for the production branch
gitflow.default.production.markdownDescription:
**🌿 Default Branch Names**

Default name for the production branch. Usually 'master' or 'main' depending on your repository setup.

gitflow.default.task.description: 🌿 Branch Names: Default prefix for task branches
gitflow.default.task.markdownDescription:
**🌿 Default Branch Names**

Default prefix for task branches. Tasks are sub-branches created from features for specific work items.

gitflow.cardIntegration.enabled.description: 🎫 Card Integration: Enable card-based branch naming
gitflow.cardIntegration.enabled.markdownDescription:
**🎫 Card Integration Setup**

Enable integration with project management tools (Jira, Azure DevOps, GitHub Issues, etc.). When enabled, branch names will include card/ticket numbers for better traceability.

gitflow.cardIntegration.required.description: 🎫 Card Integration: Make card ID mandatory
gitflow.cardIntegration.required.markdownDescription:
**🎫 Card ID Requirement**

When enabled, card ID will be required for all new branches. When disabled, card ID is optional and traditional branch names are still allowed.

gitflow.cardIntegration.prefix.description: 🎫 Card Integration: Card prefix (e.g., JIRA-, PROJ-, or empty for numbers only)
gitflow.cardIntegration.prefix.markdownDescription:
**🎫 Card Prefix Configuration**

Prefix to add before card IDs. Examples:
- `JIRA-` → JIRA-123456
- `PROJ-` → PROJ-789
- Empty → 123456 (numbers only)

gitflow.cardIntegration.format.markdownDescription:
**🎫 Branch Name Template**

Template for generating branch names. Available placeholders:
- `{type}` - Branch type (feature, task, hotfix) **[Required]**
- `{name}` - Branch description **[Required]**
- `{prefix}` - Card prefix (optional)
- `{cardId}` - Card ID number (optional)

Example: `{type}/{prefix}{cardId}-{name}` → `feature/JIRA-123456-new-login`
gitflow.cardIntegration.format.patternErrorMessage: Template must include both {type} and {name} placeholders

gitflow.cardIntegration.validation.description: 🎫 Card Integration: Regex pattern for card ID validation
gitflow.cardIntegration.validation.markdownDescription:
**🎫 Card ID Validation**

Regular expression to validate card IDs. Examples:
- `^[0-9]+$` - Numbers only (123456)
- `^[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{4}$` - Two letters + 4 numbers (AB1234)
- `^[0-9]{6}$` - Exactly 6 digits (123456)

scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run lint
